categories.main_business_segments: First Hawaiian, Inc. operates through three main business segments: Retail Banking, Commercial Banking, and Treasury and Other. Retail Banking serves consumers and small businesses with deposit, lending, and wealth management services. Commercial Banking focuses on middle-market and large businesses, offering commercial loans, real estate lending, and dealer financing. Treasury and Other includes asset/liability management, investment securities, and corporate functions.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: FHB relies on a combination of traditional branch banking, digital banking platforms (online and mobile), and a recently upgraded core banking system. The bank employs robust risk management, credit scoring, and underwriting systems, as well as technology-driven solutions for payments, card processing, and wealth management. Cybersecurity and data protection are emphasized, with ongoing investments in IT infrastructure and compliance systems.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The bank primarily serves consumers, small businesses, and middle-market to large commercial clients. Key markets include individuals seeking deposit and lending products, auto dealers, real estate developers, and businesses requiring commercial loans, treasury, and wealth management services. The bank also provides trust, investment, and insurance services to high-net-worth individuals and institutional clients.
categories.geographic_coverage: FHB is headquartered in Honolulu, Hawaii, and operates 51 branches across Hawaii (46), Guam (3), and Saipan (2). The majority of its business is concentrated in Hawaii, with additional lending and leasing activities on the U.S. mainland, particularly in California, and select commercial real estate and dealer financing activities in Guam and Saipan.
categories.supply_chain_position: FHB operates as a downstream, customer-facing financial institution, providing end-user banking, lending, and wealth management services. It acts as a direct intermediary between depositors and borrowers, and also offers payment processing and investment services, positioning itself at the retail and commercial end of the financial services supply chain.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The bank's strategic priorities include deepening customer relationships, expanding digital and mobile banking capabilities, maintaining strong risk management, and investing in talent development and diversity. FHB emphasizes innovation in customer experience, operational efficiency, and cybersecurity, while also focusing on organic growth in its core markets and prudent capital management.
categories.revenue_model: FHB generates revenue primarily through net interest income from loans and leases, as well as noninterest income from service charges, card fees, wealth management, trust services, and merchant processing. Additional revenue streams include investment securities, insurance, and fee-based services. The bank also earns income from its investment portfolio and bank-owned life insurance.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: FHB faces competition from local and national commercial banks, savings banks, credit unions, and non-bank financial services firms, including fintechs. Major competitors include Bank of Hawaii, American Savings Bank, and large mainland banks targeting Hawaii. FHB is the largest full-service bank headquartered in Hawaii, with a leading market share in assets, loans, and deposits.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2022, FHB had $24.6 billion in assets, $14.1 billion in loans and leases, $21.7 billion in deposits, and $2.3 billion in stockholders’ equity. Net income for 2022 was $265.7 million, with a return on average assets of 1.06% and a return on average equity of 11.44%. The bank has demonstrated stable profitability and asset growth, with a focus on maintaining strong capital and credit quality.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: FHB differentiates itself through its deep local market knowledge, long-standing customer relationships, comprehensive product suite, and high service quality. The bank emphasizes a relationship-based approach, community engagement, and a strong service culture, supported by digital innovation and a robust branch network. Its leading market position in Hawaii and focus on customer experience are key competitive advantages.
